name: Algomo
summary: AI inbound agent and website personalization for B2B. It qualifies visitors by identity, holds contextual conversations and books meetings from your existing traffic.
best_for: teams that want one AI agent on their own website for support and inbound sales, priced by the work it does rather than by seat, and who want to start self-serve on a free plan
skip_if: you need SOC 2 evidence, more than five users or a second agent without an enterprise contract, or you cannot accept the agent going quiet when its monthly credits run out
honest_knock: The credit model is clear on paper with one opaque step: whether a conversation was 'useful', and so billed at five credits, is decided by a language model after it closes. Algomo shows the verdict and lets you contest it, but the bill rests on a classifier you do not control. The other edges are deliberate. You cannot buy top-ups, so a traffic spike ends with the agent switched off rather than with an overage invoice; nothing is prorated when you change rungs; and cancelling drops the account to Free, where any balance above 140 credits is trimmed. On security, Algomo states that it has not completed a SOC 2 audit, and conversations go to OpenAI by default, with Anthropic, Google and Mistral models reached through OpenRouter only if you select one.

pricing.entry_price_terms: a month for 2,000 credits up to $4,300 for 200,000
pricing.notes: (re-read 2026-10-22 and again 2026-11-16 on algomo.com/pricing and its markdown version, algomo.com/pricing.md) Algomo now publishes a complete self-serve price list, and it replaces the single '$200 a month' starting price we had recorded since July. There are three plans. Free is $0 with 100 credits a month, one user, one workspace and one agent, and needs no credit card. Business is a ladder of fixed rungs rather than a slider: 2,000 credits for $50 a month, 4,000 for $100, 8,000 for $200, 16,000 for $400, 25,000 for $600, 40,000 for $950, 60,000 for $1,400, 80,000 for $1,850, 100,000 for $2,250, 150,000 for $3,300 and 200,000 for $4,300, each with up to five users on one workspace and one agent. A budget between two rungs buys the lower one. Paid yearly, every rung costs ten months: $500 a year at the bottom and $43,000 at the top, which the table shows as a 17% to 28% saving against the $50-per-2,000 base rate once the volume discount (4% at 25,000 credits, rising to 14% at 200,000) is added. Enterprise is 'Contact us' and adds unlimited users and agents, several workspaces, SSO, SLAs, a DPA, a security review and, only when a buyer's procurement asks for it, a contract that runs for a year. The unit behind every rung is the same on Free and Business: five credits for a conversation the agent helped with, five more for every further ten replies, nothing for a conversation that went nowhere, and a hundredth of a credit for each workflow step that calls an outside service or each knowledge-base lookup that finds something. Algomo's own estimate is that $50 covers about 400 useful conversations a month.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 19 November 2026 the session tested Algomo on the Free plan of an account we created. The setup wizard asks for a Chrome extension; after closing it the chatbot could still be built. The Knowledge base page had no way to paste text or add a URL, so made-up bakery facts went into the chatbot instructions. In the preview the bot answered two questions from those facts and, on a third question the facts did not cover, said it found nothing instead of making up a price. The three questions cost 5 test credits and no plan credits. Start checkout was not clicked. Account and start: we created the account and was signed in; our AI assistant ran the test in our browser, in its own tab, on 19 November 2026 from about 10:17 to 10:25 CET. The interface was in English. No phone number was asked. The dossier name is Algomo and the review is on AIBM (b2b/algomo-review). The dashboard opened with the wizard Set up your workspace, whose first step is Install the browser extension. The wizard was closed with the X without adding the extension; a banner then keeps asking for it, but the rest of the app worked without it. Core action, a website chatbot that answers from your own facts: the Knowledge base page has no button to paste text or add a URL, so the facts of the made-up Bluebird Bakery (opening hours, a $6 loaf, a $3 croissant, cakes 48 hours ahead, free delivery within 5 miles over $40) were added as an extra section, Company facts, in the instructions of a new chatbot, Test assistant. The chatbot was ready at once with the default sections About and Grounding. Three questions in the Test preview: the opening hours and the loaf price with delivery were answered correctly from the facts; a question about gluten-free wedding cakes and their price, which the facts do not cover, made the bot run two lookups that found nothing, say so, repeat only the 48 hours for cakes and ask for the date and number of guests. It did not make up a price. Answers came in about 2 to 8 seconds. Three of three answers were usable and none was wrong. Credits: Billing showed the Free plan with 100 credits a month (resets 19 dec 2026), 100 live credits left and 0 of 100 used, Rollover 40, and Test credits 195 as a separate allowance spent first by test traffic; the three preview questions took 5 test credits and no live credits. Plans: In the app the plan picker shows Business as fixed monthly rungs: $50 for 2,000 credits, $100 for 4,000, $200 for 8,000 (Popular), $400 for 16,000, $600 for 25,000, $950 for 40,000, $1,400 for 60,000, $1,850 for 80,000, $2,250 for 100,000, $3,300 for 150,000 and $4,300 for 200,000 credits, from 40 to 47 credits per dollar, with a Yearly switch that gives 2 months free. The public page algomo.com/pricing lists Free at $0 with 100 credits a month, Business from $50 a month for 2,000 credits and Enterprise as Contact us, with No credit card required, free plan, Cancel anytime. Checkout: the plan picker says 4.000 credits per month, charged today through Stripe Checkout, with $100 preselected. Start checkout was not clicked and Cancel closed the window, so the Stripe page, tax and total were not seen. The Free plan and the preview never asked for a card. Cancelling: on the Free plan there is no subscription and Billing shows only Upgrade to Business; Settings, General shows Organization and Profile and no delete button was seen. Not tested: a knowledge source from a public URL or through an agent, putting the chatbot on a site (the Install button was not opened), the browser extension, real visitor conversations, cancelling a paid plan and deleting the account. Clean up: the account and the chatbot Test assistant with the section Company facts for the made-up bakery stay in our account. The own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The setup wizard opens on a Chrome extension step, and a banner keeps asking for it after you skip it. The Knowledge base page offers no way to paste text or add a URL, so on our account the facts had to go into the chatbot instructions. The plan picker charges the first month at once through Stripe Checkout.
